questions.q: How many branches does a Condition action produce?
options: One, which either runs or is skipped
Two: If yes and If no
Three: If yes, If no, and If error
As many as there are comparisons inside it
questions.explain: A Condition action always evaluates to exactly two branches — If yes (true) and If no (false) — like an if/else statement.

questions.q: What does Apply to each require as its input?
options: A single string value
An array, which it iterates once per item
Another flow to call
A variable that must already be an integer
questions.explain: Apply to each takes an array (such as a set of attachments or table rows) and runs its inner actions once for each item in that array.

questions.q: By default, how does Apply to each run its iterations?
options: In parallel, always
Sequentially, one after another
In a random order determined at runtime
Only once, regardless of array size
questions.explain: Apply to each runs sequentially by default. It can be switched to run in parallel, but sequential avoids race conditions when a variable is updated inside the loop.

questions.q: Where can a variable be initialized in a Power Automate flow?
options: Only inside a Condition's If yes branch
Only inside an Apply to each loop
Only at the top level of the flow, never inside a Condition, Scope, or loop
Anywhere, with no restriction
questions.explain: Initialize variable can only be used at the flow's top level. A variable needed inside a loop must be initialized before the loop starts, then changed with Set or Increment inside it.

questions.q: Which action would you use to add a number to an existing integer variable's current value?
options: Initialize variable
Append to array variable
Increment variable
Apply to each
questions.explain: Increment variable adds a constant value to an existing integer or float variable. Initialize variable only declares a variable; it can't be used again to change it later.
